A sprint engine is a lightweight, automatic workflow orchestrator that transforms a collection of user‑defined atomic jobs (functions, scripts, or API calls) into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) and manages their execution. It discovers data dependencies between jobs, schedules them for parallel or sequential runs based on those dependencies, and monitors each job’s status, retries any failures, and caches intermediate results. The engine also exposes a minimal API for triggering runs, inspecting progress, and debugging, allowing teams to focus on crafting the individual jobs while the sprint engine guarantees correct, efficient, and reproducible execution of the entire pipeline.
